draft.title: What changes a price
card: A price can change when demand changes. If more buyers want a product, its price tends to rise. If fewer want it, the price tends to fall.
A price can change when supply changes. If sellers offer less of a product, its price tends to rise. If they offer more, it tends to fall.
Costs of making a product matter too. If a business pays more for materials or wages, it may raise its price to cover them.
Competition also affects price. When many sellers compete for the same buyers, they may cut prices to win sales.
draft.remember: Demand, supply, costs and competition can all push a price up or down.

a.q: A heatwave in Perth leads many more people to want ice cream. What is the most likely effect on the price of ice cream?
opts: It rises, because demand has increased
It falls, because demand has increased
It rises, because competition has increased
It falls, because costs have increased
a.why: More buyers wanting a product tends to push its price up. A rise in demand does not usually lower the price.
a.clue: Think about what more buyers means for sellers.

b.q: Many new bakeries open on one street in Darwin, all selling similar bread. What is the most likely effect on the price of bread there?
opts: It falls, as bakeries compete for buyers
It rises, as bakeries have higher costs
It rises, as there are more bakeries to buy from
It stays the same, as competition has no effect
b.why: With more sellers chasing the same buyers, bakeries may cut prices to win sales. Costs are not said to have changed, so a rise is not the likely effect.
b.clue: What might sellers do to win buyers from each other?

a.best: It rises, because demand has increased

b.best: It falls, as bakeries compete for buyers
